items.q: A 62-year-old man presents with sudden vertigo, dysphagia, hoarseness, ipsilateral facial numbness, ipsilateral Horner syndrome, and loss of pain and temperature sensation over the contralateral trunk and extremities. An occlusion of which artery is responsible?
items.exp: This is classic lateral medullary syndrome (Wallenberg syndrome), caused by occlusion of the posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA) or vertebral artery. The nucleus ambiguus damage causes dysphagia and hoarseness; the spinal trigeminal nucleus lesion causes ipsilateral facial sensory loss; descending sympathetics cause Horner syndrome; and spinothalamic tract infarction causes contralateral body sensory loss.
r: Incorrect. AICA infarction causes lateral pontine syndrome with facial paralysis and hearing loss.
Correct. PICA occlusion causes lateral medullary syndrome (Wallenberg syndrome).
Incorrect. Anterior spinal artery occlusion causes medial medullary syndrome with tongue deviation.
Incorrect. Superior cerebellar artery occlusion does not cause dysphagia or hoarseness.
items.kp: Lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome is caused by PICA occlusion; nucleus ambiguus damage causes dysphagia and hoarseness.
